lines.cap: **Narrator:** This is Kavya. She is twelve. Saturday, nine a.m., Studio 5, where they film game shows.
**Benny:** Welcome to **Singapore's Most Average Family**! The most average family wins **$1000**!
**Dad:** We are not average. We are **above** average.
**Mum:** Darling. One thousand dollars.
**Dad:** We are **extremely** average.
**Kavya:** Dad, you can't be extremely average. That's the whole point.
**Narrator:** But this documentary is about the four characters living inside the scoreboard. They decide what average means.
**Mean:** Mean. Head of averages. I add everything up and share it out **fairly**. Everybody gets the same.
**Ah Boy:** You look a bit mean.
**Mean:** I am not mean. I am **the** Mean. There is a difference.
**Otto:** Hellooo! Is this the average show? Can I join in?
**Mean:** Absolutely not. That is an **outlier**. Nobody let him near my numbers.
**Narrator:** Perfectly Average. Episode 19: The Most Average Family in Singapore.
**Benny:** Round one! How many times did you each **check your phone** this morning?
**Benny:** Kavya **7**, Mum **3**, Dad **9**, Ah Boy **4**, Priya **3**, and Mr Tan... **10**?
**Mr Tan:** I have a camera on my cat, Pythagoras. He was napping. It was riveting.
**Mean:** The **mean**: add them all up, **36**. Six people, so 36 ÷ 6 = **6**. **Total ÷ number of values**.
**Dad:** The **median** is the middle. The middle of the board is **9** and **4**. So **6.5**!
**Medi:** Medi. The median. **Line up!** In **order** first! **3, 3, 4, 7, 9, 10**.
**Medi:** Six values: the **(6 + 1) ÷ 2 = 3.5th** value, halfway between **4** and **7**. Median **5.5**.
**Mo:** Mo! The **mode**! The **most** common value! **3** appears **twice**. Three is **trending**!
**Ranger:** Ranger. The **range**: largest minus smallest, 10 − 3 = **7**. **One** number. I measure **spread**.
**Benny:** Everybody! Hey diddle diddle, the **median's the middle**, you **add and divide** for the **mean**!
**Ah Boy:** The **mode** is the one that appears the **most**, and the **range** is the **difference** between!
**Mr Tan:** Bonus! My holiday in Seoul. Overnight lows: **−3, 2, −5, 0, −3, 4, −2** °C.
**Ranger:** Never negative. **4 − (−5) = 4 + 5 = 9** degrees.
**Mr Tan:** Seoul was so cold, even my **mean** was negative.
**Benny:** A word from our sponsor! **Boba Boss** bubble tea is hiring! **Mean monthly pay: $4000!**
**Mum:** Four thousand dollars? I'm applying. Today.
**Kavya:** Wait. The six workers earn **$2400** to **$3000**. And the owner...
**Otto:** Hi! I'm Otto! The owner's pay: **$12 200**! I'm an **outlier**: much bigger than the rest!
**Mean:** Total **$28 000**, ÷ 7 = **$4000**. True! But he's dragging me **above every single worker**!
**Medi:** I don't move. I only care about **position**. The 4th of 7: **$2600**. The mode, **$2500**, stays put too.
**Ranger:** Me, he **stretches**: 12 200 − 2400 = **$9800**. A huge range.
**Ah Boy:** Can we just delete Otto?
**Kavya:** Don't just delete an outlier. Ask **why** it's there. A mistake? Fix it. Real? Keep it, and use the **median**.
**Otto:** Thank you! I feel very seen.
**Mean:** But I use **every** value! Isn't the mean **always** best?
**Medi:** Not with outliers. Then the **median** wins.
**Benny:** Round two: **which average**? A shoe shop orders most of one size.
**Priya:** The **mode**! The most popular size. A mean shoe size like **5.37** doesn't even exist!
**Mum:** Flat prices, with a few outliers? The **median**. Test marks with **no** outliers? The **mean**.
**Mo:** That's **me**, the **mode**! It's also your **fastest** time. Very flattering.
**Dad:** I choose the mode.
**Mean:** That is not **fair**.
**Narrator:** Round three: a quiz, five rounds, each out of 20. Priya's parents are still parking.
**Priya:** Team captain. My mean for four rounds is **15**. I want a mean of **16**. So **17** on the last one?
**Mean:** Means can't be added. **Totals** can. **Total = mean × number of values**.
**Kavya:** So far: **4 × 15 = 60**. Needed: **5 × 16 = 80**. So the last round needs **80 − 60 = 20**.
**Priya:** Twenty? That's **full marks**!
**Benny:** Quick-fire! The mean of five numbers is **8**. Four of them are **3, 7, 9** and **12**. The fifth?
**Dad:** Required total: **5 × 8 = 40**. Known total: **31**. Missing: **40 − 31 = 9**. **Above** average.
**Auntie Rose:** Auntie Rose! I came to cheer! But don't tell them my **age**, ah!
**Benny:** A new member! Team Kavya's four had a mean age of **26**. With Auntie Rose, it's **33**!
**Kavya:** Old total: **4 × 26 = 104**. New total: **5 × 33 = 165**. So Auntie Rose is **165 − 104 = 61**.
**Auntie Rose:** Aiyo. Mathematics is very rude.
**Benny:** The audience! Left side: **20** people, mean score **62**. Right side: **30** people, mean **72**.
**Ah Boy:** Halfway! **67**!
**Mean:** Only if the groups are the **same size**. Totals: 1240 + 2160 = **3400**, ÷ 50 = **68**.
**Ranger:** And if everyone gets **2** bonus marks? Mean, median and mode go **up 2**. My range stays **the same**.
**Narrator:** Round four. The show surveyed **20 flats** on Kavya's floor of Block 208.
**Dad:** Easy. 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 15. Divide by 5. Mean: **3**!
**Ah Boy:** No! Add the flats: **20**. Divide by 5: **4**!
**Sigma:** SIGMA! Greek for **add them all up**! You're **both wrong**!
**Sigma:** It's a list of **20** numbers. Add an **fx** column: **value × frequency**.
**Mean:** Mean = **total of fx ÷ total of f** = 56 ÷ 20 = **2.8** people per flat. Divide by the **flats**, not the rows.
**Medi:** Median: the **(20 + 1) ÷ 2 = 10.5th** value. Running totals: **3**, **9**, **14**. Values 10 to 14 are all **3**s.
**Kavya:** So the 10th and the 11th are both **3**. The median is **3 people**.
**Priya:** Mode is **6**! It's the biggest number in the table!
**Mo:** Bestie, no. **6** is the **frequency**. The mode is the **value**: **2 people**.
**Ranger:** Range: use the **values**, not the frequencies. 5 − 1 = **4** people.
**Mr Tan:** My flat: one person. And Pythagoras.
**Sigma:** Cats are not data.
**Mr Tan:** Pythagoras disagrees.
**Narrator:** Round five. Fifteen audience members were timed on their way to the studio.
**Benny:** Here's a **stem-and-leaf diagram**! **Key: 1 | 5** means **15 minutes**.
**Ah Boy:** It's a plant!
**Medi:** It's **better** than a plant. It's **already in order**.
**Medi:** **15** leaves, so the median is the **8th**. Stem 0 has **2**, stem 1 has **5** more: that's **7**.
**Medi:** So the 8th is the **first leaf** on stem 2: **20 minutes**.
**Mo:** Mode: three **5**s on the **same stem**: **15 minutes**. A 5 on stem 2 would be 25!
**Ranger:** Range: last value minus first value: **45 − 8 = 37 minutes**.
**Narrator:** The prize: twelve durians, labelled with a stem-and-leaf diagram.
**Ah Boy:** **1 | 4**! A **14 kg** durian! We're rich!
**Kavya:** Read the **key** first! **2 | 5** means **2.5 kg**. So 1 | 4 is just **1.4 kg**.
**Medi:** **12** durians. Median: halfway between the 6th and 7th, **2.2** and **2.5**: **2.35 kg**.
**Mo:** Mode **1.6 kg**: three of them! Range **3.8 − 1.4 = 2.4 kg**.
**Dad:** Twelve durians. In a closed studio. With air-con.
**Mum:** The smell is definitely an outlier.
**Narrator:** The final. Each team picks **one** player for the beanbag toss. Five practice sessions, ten throws each.
**Dad:** Mine: **10, 2, 9, 3, 6**. A **ten**! Clearly above average.
**Ranger:** Not the same **spread**. Mum: 7 − 5 = **2**. Dad: 10 − 2 = **8**.
**Kavya:** Mum is **consistent**. Dad is **variable**: brilliant one day, terrible the next.
**Dad:** I prefer **exciting**.
**Mr Tan:** To compare data sets, make **two** comparisons: an **average** and the **spread**. In **context**.
**Kavya:** **Centre**, **Spread**, **Story**. On average, Mum and Dad scored the **same**: a mean of **6** each.
**Kavya:** But Mum's scores were **more consistent**, because her range was smaller: **2** compared with **8**.
**Benny:** Breaking news! Viewers' poll: Team Priya, mean rating **9** out of 10. Team Kavya, only **7**!
**Kavya:** How many people voted for Team Priya?
**Priya:** **Three.** My mum, my dad and me. They voted from the car park.
**Mr Tan:** A sample of **three** is far too small. The data **suggest**; they don't **prove**.
**Narrator:** A stretch round, while the judges count. Forty audience members ran a fun run.
**Kavya:** No exact times, so use each group's **midpoint**: **25, 35, 45, 55**. Times the frequencies: **150, 525, 495, 440**. Total **1610**.
**Mean:** **1610 ÷ 40 = 40.25** minutes. Only an **estimate**: we pretended everyone finished on a midpoint.
**Sigma:** WRONG! You ignored the **frequencies**! Fifteen runners outweigh six!
**Mo:** **Modal class**: **30 ≤ t < 40**. The most popular group!
**Ranger:** And my range? Less than 60 − 20 = **40**. Exactly? Nobody knows. Very relaxing.

chapters.title: The scoreboard saves you some marks

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Before the results, the scoreboard would like to save you some marks.
**Medi:** One. Put the data **in order** before you find the median. **In ORDER!**
**Sigma:** Two. In a frequency table, divide by the **total frequency**, not the number of rows!
**Mo:** Three. The mode is the **value**, not the frequency. **2 people**, not **6 flats**.
**Ranger:** Four. The range is **one** number. **8**, not '2 to 10'.
**Kavya:** Five. Compare an **average** AND the **range**, in **context**. Two sentences.
**Ah Boy:** Six. Read the **key**. My fourteen kilogram durian was one point four. I'm still sad.
**Narrator:** Perfectly Average will return.
**Benny:** And Singapore's Most Average Family is... **Team Tan**!
**Mr Tan:** A family of one. My mean: me. My median: me. My range: **zero**. Perfectly consistent.
**Ah Boy:** What about Pythagoras?
**Mr Tan:** Cats are not data.
**Dad:** We lost to one man. I am still **above** average.
**Otto:** Group hug!
**Mean:** Not fair... I am being dragged... towards the outlier...
